mainTopic: When private fasting is proper, the תלמיד חכם exception, and the rules of partial fasts and תפילת תענית
overview: This amud first finishes a debate about whether taking on a private fast is good or harmful. The גמרא resolves a contradiction: fasting is holy for someone whose body can handle it, and harmful for someone who cannot. ריש לקיש calls a faster a חסיד. רב ששת and רב ירמיה בר אבא say a Torah student or תלמיד חכם should not fast, because it weakens his learning. רב ירמיה בר אבא also rules that in בבל only תשעה באב is a full public fast. The גמרא then returns to the משנה. רב הונא rules that an individual who ate all night still says תפילת תענית the next day, but one who just kept fasting into the night does not. רב יוסף asks for רב הונא's reason, and אביי explains that those night hours were never accepted in advance. Finally, מר עוקבא is asked three questions in גינזק, and the בית מדרש answers all of them: partial fasts count and get the fast prayer, gentile wine jars are permitted after twelve months, and משה served the מילואים days in a white robe. The amud ends as רב חסדא begins a statement that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A contradiction: holiness dwells inside a person's body
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a teaching of רבי אלעזר that a person should see holiness as dwelling inside his body. That clashes with the idea that one who fasts is called קדוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: [But רבי אלעזר said: A person should always see himself] as if something holy is dwelling inside his innards, as it says: 'The Holy One is in your midst, and I will not come into the city' (הושע 11:9)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is raising a contradiction. Earlier, fasting was praised as making a person קדוש. Here, a statement of רבי אלעזר suggests you should not afflict your body, because something holy lives inside it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If holiness dwells inside the body, then weakening the body through fasting damages something holy. So this statement seems to discourage fasting. That contradicts the earlier claim that a faster is praised as קדוש, and the גמרא must now reconcile the two.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The words before it (roughly 'רבי אלעזר said: a person should always view himself') come earlier. The exclamation mark shows this is a challenge, not a new teaching.

phrases.english: as if something holy dwells within his innards,
as it is said:
'In your midst is the Holy One, and I will not come into the city'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the debate earlier about whether one who fasts is a sinner or holy.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that one who fasts is called קדוש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If holiness dwells in the body, afflicting the body through fasting harms that holiness. So fasting should be discouraged, not praised.

steps.title: It depends on whether the person can handle the fast
steps.stepSummary: No contradiction: fasting is praiseworthy for someone who can bear it, and harmful for someone who cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one is where he is able to afflict himself; that one is where he is not able to afflict himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by splitting it into two different kinds of people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a person's body can handle a fast without harm, his fasting is holy and praiseworthy. If he cannot handle it, the fast damages the 'holiness inside him,' and he should not fast. Both statements are true, each for a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (introduces a resolution)
This one… that one (splits two cases)
To afflict / cause distress to himself

steps.whatToRemember: Private fasting is good only when a person's body can truly handle it. Otherwise it harms him.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is where he is able to afflict himself,
that one is where he is not able to afflict himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that one statement praises fasting and the other forbids it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Fasting is praiseworthy for one who can bear it. It is improper for one whose body cannot handle it.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: one who fasts is called pious
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש adds a third view: a person who fasts is called a חסיד, based on a פסוק in משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: He is called pious, as it says: 'The pious man does good to (or: holds back from) his soul, while he who troubles his flesh is cruel' (משלי 11:17).
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives his own opinion on fasting: the faster is called a חסיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word גומל can also mean 'weaning' or 'holding back.' So 'גומל נפשו' is read as 'one who holds his soul back from food,' and the פסוק calls such a person an איש חסד. This is a new label, alongside the earlier views of 'sinner' and 'holy.'

keyTerms.meaning: Holds back / weans his soul (read here as abstaining from food)

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
he is called pious,
as it is said: 'The pious man restrains his soul,
and he who troubles his flesh, etc.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another opinion to the list of views on the status of one who fasts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who fasts is called a חסיד.

steps.title: רב ששת: a yeshiva student who fasts loses his meal
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says a yeshiva student who fasts has, in effect, let a dog eat his meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: This yeshiva student who sits in a fast, let a dog eat his meal.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives a sharp statement against fasting for a Torah student.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fasting weakens the student, so he learns less. That makes his fast a loss with no gain. It is as if a dog ate his food: the meal is gone, and nothing good came of it. This narrows the praise of fasting: for a learner, the cost to his learning outweighs the benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: A student of the study hall / yeshiva student

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי בַּר בֵּי רַב דְּיָתֵיב בְּתַעֲנִיתָא —
phrases.english: this yeshiva student who sits in a fast —
let a dog eat his meal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת הַאי בַּר בֵּי רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from fasting in general to the special case of a Torah student.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Torah student should not fast, since he loses learning and gains nothing.

steps.title: In בבל, only תשעה באב is a full public fast
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה בר אבא rules that בבל has no fully stringent communal fast except תשעה באב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה בר אבא said: There is no communal fast in בבל except תשעה באב alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling that limits how strict public fasts are outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Other fasts in בבל are treated with the rules of an individual's fast, not the full stringencies of a תענית ציבור. Only תשעה באב has the complete severity of a public fast. The fasts still exist. What changes is how strict their rules are.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean there are no other fast days in בבל. It means they do not carry the full stringencies of a public fast.

phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said:
there is no communal fast in Babylonia
except the Ninth of Av alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אֵין תַּעֲנִית צִיבּוּר בְּבָבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from private fasting to the status of public fasts in בבל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only תשעה באב has full communal-fast stringency in בבל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling affects practical הלכה for fasts outside ארץ ישראל, such as which stringencies apply on them.

steps.title: A תלמיד חכם may not fast
steps.stepSummary: Quoting ריש לקיש, רב ירמיה בר אבא rules that a Torah scholar may not take on a fast, because it weakens his service of Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה בר אבא said in the name of ריש לקיש: A Torah scholar is not permitted to sit in a fast, because he reduces the work of Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: A second statement of רב ירמיה בר אבא, this time in ריש לקיש's name, forbids a תלמיד חכם from fasting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fasting drains strength, and a scholar needs his strength for Torah and מצוות, which are 'מלאכת שמים.' So for him, fasting is not merely unhelpful (like רב ששת said) but actually not permitted. Notice that ריש לקיש called a faster a חסיד, yet he excludes the scholar.

keyTerms.meaning: The work of Heaven (Torah study and מצוות)

steps.whatToRemember: Fasting can be pious for an ordinary person, but a תלמיד חכם should not fast because it weakens his Torah learning.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said that Reish Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין תַּלְמִיד חָכָם רַשַּׁאי לֵישֵׁב בְּתַעֲנִית,
phrases.english: a Torah scholar is not permitted to sit in a fast,
because he diminishes the work of Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens רב ששת's point about Torah students into a full prohibition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד חכם may not take on a fast, because it reduces his service of Heaven.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: eating after dark before a fast
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'they eat and drink after dark' to open a new discussion.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה said:] They eat and drink after it gets dark, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is returning to the משנה and quoting it. This sets up the next statement, about an individual's fast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that during the first set of fasts, people may eat the night before, and the fast begins only in the morning. Quoting this line signals that the coming teaching of רב הונא builds on this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc. (the quote continues in the משנה)

phrases.english: They eat and drink from when it gets dark, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the general discussion of fasting and returns to the text of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During the first fasts, eating is allowed on the night before the fast.

steps.title: An individual who ate all night still says the fast prayer
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that an individual who accepted a fast says תפילת תענית the next day, even if he ate the entire night before.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זעירא said in the name of רב הונא: An individual who accepted a fast upon himself, even if he ate and drank the whole night, the next day he prays the fast-day prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: Building on the משנה's rule that you may eat the night before, רב הונא teaches that eating at night does not cancel the fast day's status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fast is a daytime fast, so eating at night does not damage it. Therefore the next day still counts as a real fast day. He says the fast-day prayer, such as עננו.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זְעֵירָא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rav Huna said:
an individual who accepted a fast upon himself,
even if he ate and drank the entire night —
the next day he prays the prayer of a fast.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זְעֵירָא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the משנה's 'eating after dark' rule to the case of an individual's fast.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating at night does not cancel the next day's fast. He says תפילת תענית the next day.

steps.title: One who fasted through the night does not say the fast prayer
steps.stepSummary: The second half of רב הונא's ruling: if someone kept fasting through the night after his fast day, he does not say the fast prayer the next morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he 'slept in his fast,' he does not pray the prayer of a fast.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא adds the opposite case. A person simply kept fasting overnight after his fast day ended.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After his accepted fast day ended, he kept fasting through the night. For those extra hours, רב הונא rules that he does not say תפילת תענית the next morning. רב הונא gives no reason here. The next step has רב יוסף ask for the reason, and in Step 11 אביי explains that those night hours were never accepted in advance.

keyTerms.meaning: Spent the night in his fast (kept fasting overnight)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume that fasting longer means you say more fast prayers. Here, fasting on into the night does not earn the fast prayer the next morning. The reason is discussed in Steps 10–11.
steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא: eating the night before doesn't cancel the next day's fast prayer, and fasting on through the night doesn't earn a fast prayer the next morning.

phrases.english: if he spent the night in his fast —
he does not pray the prayer of a fast.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב הונא's statement with the contrasting case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who keeps fasting into the night after his fast day does not say תפילת תענית the next morning.

steps.title: רב יוסף asks for the reason behind רב הונא's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks why רב הונא said that fasting into the night does not earn the fast prayer the next morning. He offers two possible reasons.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: What does רב הונא hold? Does he hold that a fast of only some hours is not a fast at all? Or does he hold that a fast of some hours is a real fast, but someone who fasts only for hours does not say the fast prayer?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף is trying to find the reason behind רב הונא's ruling from Step 9. He gives two possible explanations and asks which one is right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא ruled that a person who kept fasting into the night does not say the fast prayer the next morning. Option 1: a fast of only some hours does not count as a fast at all. Option 2: it does count, but it is too small to earn תפלת תענית.

keyTerms.meaning: one may fast for (only) some hours, and it counts as a fast

steps.confusionAlert: Both of רב יוסף's options lead to the same practical result: no fast prayer the next morning. The question is only about the REASON. The reason matters because it decides other cases.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
What does Rav Huna hold?
Does he hold: one does not fast for hours,
phrases.notes: A partial-day fast is not a fast at all.

phrases.english: or perhaps: one does fast for hours —

phrases.aramaic: וְהַמִּתְעַנֶּה לְשָׁעוֹת אֵינוֹ מִתְפַּלֵּל תְּפִלַּת תַּעֲנִית?
phrases.english: but one who fasts for hours does not pray the fast prayer?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מַאי קָסָבַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רב הונא's ruling in Step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is רב הונא's ruling based on partial fasts not counting at all, or on partial fasts not earning the fast prayer?

steps.title: אביי: partial fasts count, but unplanned night hours do not
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects both of רב יוסף's options. Partial fasts count and do get the fast prayer. The night hours are different only because they were never accepted in advance.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Really, רב הונא holds that one may fast for hours, and one who fasts for hours does say the fast prayer. But here it is different, because these night hours were not accepted on himself from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב יוסף with a third explanation. רב הונא's ruling has nothing to do with partial fasts in general.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, a fast of some hours counts and even gets תפלת תענית. A private fast must be accepted beforehand. The extra night hours were never accepted, so they are not a real fast, and no prayer is said for them.

keyTerms.meaning: accepted upon himself from the start

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a private fast depends on accepting it in advance (קבלת תענית). Simply not eating, without accepting a fast, does not make a fast in הלכה.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם קָסָבַר רַב הוּנָא מִתְעַנִּין לְשָׁעוֹת,
phrases.english: Actually, Rav Huna holds one may fast for hours,
and one who fasts for hours does pray the fast prayer.
But here it is different,
because there are hours of the night
that he did not accept upon himself from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: לְעוֹלָם קָסָבַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's question by giving a third reason.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Partial fasts count and get the fast prayer. The night hours do not, because they were never accepted beforehand.
steps.whatToRemember: A partial fast counts, but only if you accepted it in advance. Hours you just 'drifted into' do not count.

steps.title: מר עוקבא in גינזק is asked three questions he cannot answer
steps.stepSummary: The people of גינזק ask מר עוקבא three questions: about partial fasts, about gentile wine jars, and about what משה wore during the מילואים. He has no answer to any of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר עוקבא came to גינזק. They asked him: Does one fast for hours or not? He did not have an answer. Are gentiles' jars forbidden or permitted? He did not have an answer. In what clothing did משה serve all seven days of the inauguration? He did not have an answer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that raises three open questions. It is setting up the answers that come in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first question is the same issue that רב יוסף and אביי just discussed. The other two come along because they were asked at the same time. The jars question is about clay jars a gentile used for wine, which soak up forbidden wine. The third is about משה's clothing when he served as כהן during the seven days of מילואים, while אהרן and his sons were being installed.

keyTerms.meaning: he did not have it 'in his hand' (he had no answer)
gentiles' clay jars used for wine
the seven days of the inauguration of the משכן

phrases.english: Mar Ukva happened to come to Ginzak,
they asked him:

phrases.aramaic: מִתְעַנִּין לְשָׁעוֹת אוֹ אֵין מִתְעַנִּין לְשָׁעוֹת?
phrases.english: Does one fast for hours, or does one not fast for hours?
He did not have an answer.

phrases.aramaic: קַנְקַנִּין שֶׁל נׇכְרִים, אֲסוּרִין אוֹ מוּתָּרִין?
phrases.english: Gentiles' jars: are they forbidden or permitted?
He did not have an answer.
In what did Moshe serve
all seven days of the inauguration?
He did not have an answer.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר עוּקְבָא אִיקְּלַע לְגִינְזַק, בְּעוֹ מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses a story to bring up the same partial-fast question, along with two more questions.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: (1) Do partial fasts count? (2) Can gentile wine jars become permitted? (3) What did משה wear during the מילואים?

steps.title: The study hall rules: partial fasts count and get the fast prayer
steps.stepSummary: מר עוקבא asks in the בית מדרש. They rule that one may fast for hours and does say the fast prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and asked in the study hall. They told him: The הלכה is that one may fast for hours, and one does say the fast prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: The בית מדרש answers the first of the three questions with a clear ruling of הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ruling matches אביי's view from Step 11. A partial fast counts, and it even gets תפלת תענית. The case of unaccepted night hours stays an exception, not a contradiction.

phrases.english: He went and asked in the study hall.
They said to him, the halacha is:
one may fast for hours,
and one prays the fast prayer,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲזַל וּשְׁאֵיל בֵּי מִדְרְשָׁא. אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ, הִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first question from Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Partial fasts count, and one says תפלת תענית.
steps.whatToRemember: Final הלכה: מתענין לשעות. A partial fast counts and gets the fast prayer.

steps.title: Gentile wine jars become permitted after twelve months
steps.stepSummary: The בית מדרש rules that gentiles' clay wine jars become permitted after twelve months.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: gentiles' jars, after twelve months, are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The בית מדרש answers the second question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Clay jars soak up the gentile's wine, which is forbidden. After twelve months of not being used, the absorbed wine has dried out and lost its effect, so the jars may be used.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: gentiles' jars,
after twelve months — are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second question from Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The jars become permitted after twelve months.

steps.title: משה served in a white robe during the inauguration days
steps.stepSummary: The בית מדרש says משה served in a white robe during the seven days of מילואים. רב כהנא's version adds that the robe had no hem.
steps.simpleTranslation: In what did משה serve all seven days of the inauguration? In a white robe. רב כהנא taught: in a white robe that has no hem.
steps.whatsHappening: The בית מדרש answers the third question. Then the גמרא brings רב כהנא's slightly different version of the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה served as כהן during the seven days before אהרן and his sons began. He did not wear the regular בגדי כהונה; he wore a special white robe. רב כהנא adds one detail: the robe had no hem.
steps.whatToRemember: All three of גינזק's questions are answered: partial fasts count and get the prayer; jars are permitted after 12 months; משה served in a white robe (רב כהנא: with no hem).

phrases.english: In what did Moshe serve
all seven days of the inauguration —
in a white robe.
Rav Kahana teaches:
in a white robe that has no hem.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּמֶּה שִׁימֵּשׁ מֹשֶׁה כׇּל שִׁבְעַת יְמֵי הַמִּלּוּאִים — בְּחָלוּק לָבָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the third question from Step 12 and adds רב כהנא's version.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: משה served in a white robe; according to רב כהנא, one with no hem.

steps.title: רב חסדא begins a new statement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a new teaching from רב חסדא. The content of his statement comes on the next amud.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move by naming who is about to speak: רב חסדא. His actual words have not come yet; they start on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story of מר עוקבא and the people of גינזק is finished. This line opens a new teaching. Since the sugya is about fasts, expect רב חסדא to say something about when a fast counts as a real fast.

keyTerms.meaning: said; the standard word that opens a sage's statement
רב חסדא, a leading Babylonian אמורא

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a full step by itself. It only tells you who is speaking. Do not look for a ruling here; the ruling comes right after it.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
phrases.notes: Attribution formula only. It introduces the statement that follows on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the בית מדרש's answers to מר עוקבא end (Step 15), the גמרא moves to a new statement by רב חסדא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not stated on this amud. The attribution introduces רב חסדא's ruling, which appears on the next amud.
